settings.headline: It started with a kid sending a drawing to the local paper
settings.hook_paragraph_1: I was the kid who sent stuff in everywhere. The local paper had a special section and I got my writing and drawings published. A couple of my creations even made it onto Cheez TV and Saturday Disney in the morning.
settings.hook_paragraph_2: I still remember exactly how those moments felt.
settings.hook_paragraph_3: Now Tam and I are trying to give that feeling to every Aussie kid we can find.

settings.aeo_heading: How did theINmag come to be?

settings.image_alt: Photo collage of 90s Australian kids' magazine and TV show submissions.
settings.heading: Kids who sent stuff in
settings.body: Back in the 90s, kids could send their art and stories to the local paper, or to TV shows like Saturday Disney and Cheez TV. Some of them got picked. Ryan was one. Tam's sister was another. Seeing your work in print, or on the telly, made you feel like you could actually do this.

settings.image_alt: Inside an Australian primary classroom with kids' creations on the walls.
settings.heading: Years in the classroom
settings.body: Fast forward thirty years. Ryan and Tam had become teachers. Every day they watched kids make incredible things. But there was nowhere for that work to go. The classroom wall. The fridge under a magnet at home. That was it.

settings.image_alt: Notebook on a kitchen table with early planning sketches for theINmag.
settings.heading: What if we just made it?
settings.body: So they had a thought. What if we built the thing we wished existed when we were kids? A real magazine, made by Aussie kids, sent all over the country. They started planning. That was three years before the first issue ever printed.

settings.image_alt: Tam sitting with a small group of kids talking about what they like to make.
settings.heading: Listening to real kids
settings.body: For three years they sat with kids. Asked them what they liked. What they hated. What they'd actually want to read. Then they changed everything. Then they changed it again. theINmag was built by kids long before it was made for them.

settings.image_alt: Lou and Dave at a desk surrounded by magazine spread proofs.
settings.heading: The team grew
settings.body: Ryan called his cousin Dave. Dave's an illustrator and he loved the idea. He designed the first four issues. Then Lou took over. She's the reason every page has its own pattern, made from real kid artwork. Look closely - those swirls and shapes? All from kids.

settings.image_alt: Stack of printer proofs and a calculator on a kitchen table.
settings.heading: Then came the hard bit
settings.body: Printing a magazine in Australia is expensive. Really expensive. Ryan and Tam needed money to make this real. So they did something a bit wild. They sold their house. Bought a van. Spent three months turning it into a tiny home on wheels.

settings.image_alt: The van mid-conversion, plywood walls and wiring exposed.
settings.heading: A house with wheels
settings.body: The van meant two things. Money to print the magazine. And the freedom to drive anywhere in Australia. Beach towns. Bush schools. Big cities. Tiny ones. They could meet real kids, in real places, and find the next round of creators.

settings.image_alt: Baby Nora in the van, surrounded by theINmag issues.
settings.heading: Oh, and Nora arrived
settings.body: Somewhere along the way they had a baby. Her name's Nora. She's been on the road her whole life, watching her parents build a magazine and meeting kids in every state. She's pretty cool. We think so anyway.

settings.image_alt: Spread of kid creations from a recent issue of theINmag.
settings.heading: Where you fit in
settings.body: theINmag is for you. Real Aussie kids. The stuff you make right now. The ideas you've got brewing. Every page is a reflection of what kids are into - and an invitation for the next kid to give it a go.

settings.aeo_heading: Who is on the theINmag team?
settings.all_done_message: Nice work, you've met the whole team.

settings.bio: The kid sending stuff to the local paper grew up to be one half of theINmag. Tam was the other half - sporty, social, the kind of kid who organised everyone else. Total opposites. Turns out that's the perfect combo for building a magazine.
settings.fun_fact: Tam once rode her bike into a creek on the way to school. She still blames the bike.

settings.bio: Lou's been designing magazines for over a decade. She's a night owl who's absolutely obsessed with the artwork Aussie kids send in. Two creative daughters. One studio. Endless ideas.
settings.fun_fact: Lou's husband Alex owns a coffee shop, but Lou doesn't drink coffee. It makes her go a little crazy.

settings.bio: Ryan's cousin. Award-nominated picture book illustrator (look up The Nerdy Birdy). He laid out the first four issues of theINmag and set the visual feel for everything that came after.
settings.fun_fact: Dave now runs a cafe called Earlybird Espresso. Check out their logo - it's very cool.

settings.bio: Dee was the kid who wrote to the local paper so often they gave her a job. Real story. She's now an author, a mum, and the editor brain that makes sure every issue reads beautifully.
settings.fun_fact: She was the editor of Loop magazine before theINmag existed. We got lucky.

settings.bio: Twenty years in the classroom. Nina's the teacher every kid remembers - the one who actually listened. She catches the typos, the missing full stops, and the things only a great teacher would notice.
settings.fun_fact: Nina is the kind of friend who shows up. That's not really a fun fact. It's just true.

settings.bio: Adam keeps the numbers in line. Without him, we'd have had to sell the van by now. It's thanks to him we managed to print every magazine.
settings.fun_fact: A great guy and an okay footy player.

settings.bio: Chloe is the magic behind every kid creation that ends up on the page. She tweaks shadows, fixes lighting, brightens colours - so the artwork looks as good in print as it did on the kitchen table.
settings.fun_fact: Chloe's an animal lover and is obsessed with the pet shop section in the magazine.

settings.bio: Kylie makes sure theINmag reaches the right eyeballs. Social-savvy, data-driven, always five steps ahead. Also a fab mum to two little legends.
These two designed our original website. Vanlife and web design at the same time. Wild.
settings.fun_fact: A huge chunk of theINmag's look online started with them. We owe them big time.

settings.heading: And then there's the kid crew
settings.body_1: Meet Zanda, Ned and Gus. They're Tam's nephews. They pack every single order of theINmag with serious care.
settings.body_2: If you look hard at the magazine, you'll spot some of their creations in there too.

settings.heading: Branching Out
settings.body: Branching Out is our YouTube channel where we share our travels, the places we land, and what Nora's up to.

settings.aeo_heading: How can your kid be in theINmag?

settings.heading: Send something in
settings.body: Drawings, stories, photos, jokes, maths puzzles, anything. If they made it and they're proud of it, send it IN.
